lines.text: This is Kioku. In Japanese, the word means memory.
At work, meetings, documents and decisions pile up, and what matters ends up lost.
Kioku gathers everything into a personal wiki: one page per project, per person, per meeting and per decision.
Claude writes these pages and keeps them up to date, from the sources you hand it.
Then you simply ask a question. The answer comes from the wiki, with its sources.
Every piece of information follows the same path, through three layers: bronze, silver and gold. This is the medallion architecture.
To reach the gold layer, a page must pass a gate.
An independent reviewer checks where it comes from, its format, and respect for the people it mentions.
Whatever it holds back is set aside, and waits for a human decision.
Each domain, work or personal life for example, lives in its own silo, with its own reviewer and its own rules.
A local dashboard shows the whole wiki as a 3D graph: every page is a point, linked to the pages it cites.
Kioku. A working memory that no longer gets lost: reviewed, sourced, and always one question away.
